t: #3627 Maximum Median Sum of Subsequences of Size 3
o: Repeatedly remove triples, scoring each triple's median; maximize the total score. Sorted ascending, the median of a triple is its middle element. Example 1: [1,1,2,2,3,3] → medians 3 and 2 → 5. Example 2: [1,1,10,10,10,10] → 10+10 = 20. With n up to 5·10⁵ we need a direct greedy formula.
k: Sort ascending; the optimal strategy takes the largest element as a 'sacrifice' and scores the second-largest of each triple.
Concretely, score elements at sorted indices n−2, n−4, …, i.e., every second element from the top.
Exchange argument: using a bigger element as the sacrifice never helps, and each median consumes one sacrifice above it.

a.i: Sort ascending. Pair the top element with the runner-up (median = runner-up), the third with the fourth-from-top, and so on. Formally the answer is nums[n-2] + nums[n-4] + .... Any other assignment leaves some median no larger, by an exchange argument on sorted order.
s: Walk indices i = n-2, n-4, …, 0 (step −2), accumulating nums[i].
a.t: O(n log n) — dominated by sorting.

w: Once sorted, the stride-two pattern falls out of 'each median needs one strictly larger companion'. Pitfall: using 32-bit sums (values up to 1e9, n/3 terms → up to ~1.7e14). Follow-up: generalize to triples where you score the minimum, or to groups of size 5 scoring the median.
